events.title: Human Rights and Social Movements in an Era of Authoritarianism
events.description: The conference aims to take stock of the attack on human rights discourses and institutions and identify ways of advocating for human rights that are relevant to the current authoritarian era. The historic focus of many human rights organizations on the U.S. State Department (and other foreign ministries) and the United Nations and Bretton Woods institutions seems out of step with the times and compels us to think about more local and decentralized forms of protecting human rights and the rule of law. Some of the questions we are considering include: If human rights become more regionally

events.title: The Midas Monument: Behind the Facade
events.description: A landmark of Phrygian archaeology, the rock-carved facade in the highlands of western central Anatolia known as the Midas Monument has been thought to be the tomb of King Midas, or a tribute to the greatness of his kingship at the end of the eighth century BCE, or a hero shrine to the memory of King Midas and his deified mother in the sixth century BCE. Supporting this last interpretation, this lecture explores the meaning of Midas and his patron deity, the Phrygian Mother of the Gods, as they were viewed by the kings of Lydia, successors to the kingdom of Midas.Suggested readings:

events.description: The coastal mountains of greater Syria, including Mount Lebanon, are often portrayed as a zone of refuge. This idea is embedded in the historiography of the modern Lebanese state, which was established in part as a haven for allegedly persecuted minorities. This lecture steps back in time to examine the situation in Syria's coastal mountains in Late Antiquity and the Early Middle Ages, when many of these minority groups first came into existence, such as the Maronites, Druzes, and others. events.description: This lecture presents the results of two decades of archaeological research at the sites of Amheida (ancient Trimithis) and ʿAin el-Gedida in Egypt’s Dakhla Oasis. events.title: EEB 522 Seminar Series - Scott Taylor
events.description: Chickadees are familiar and widespread non-migratory birds in North America that have amazing adaptations to survive cold winters, including the ability to remember thousands of individual seed cache locations. Recovering these caches is critical for overwinter survival. Dr. Taylor will share recent results from two different studies, one focused on a chickadee hybrid zone and one focused on a single population of mountain chickadees, that both provide insights into the genetic basis of variation in spatial cognition in chickadees.

events.description: AI evaluations inform critical decisions, from the valuations of trillion-dollar companies to policies on regulating AI. Sayash Kapoor will present his FPO "The Missing Science of AI Evaluation"
events.description: Sayash Kapoor will present his FPO "The Missing Science of AI Evaluation"Date: Jul 21, 2026, 12:00 pm – 2:00 pmLocation: 306 Sherrerd Hallhttps://citp.princeton.edu/events/2026/sayash-kapoor-final-public-oral-fpo-missing-science-ai-evaluation-0Examiners: Arvind Narayanan (Adviser), Peter Henderson, and Brandon StewartReaders: Arvind Narayanan, Karthik Narasimhan, and Jessica Hullman (Northwestern Univ)AI evaluations inform critical decisions, from the valuations of trillion-dollar companies to policies on regulating AI. Yet, evaluation methods have failed to keep pace with deployment, creating an evaluation crisis where performance in the lab fails to predict real-world utility. In this talk, Kapoor discusses the evaluations crisis in a high-stakes domain: AI-based science. Across dozens of fields, from medicine to political science, he finds that flawed evaluation practices have led to overoptimistic claims about AI’s accuracy, affecting hundreds of published papers.To address these evaluation failures, Kapoor presents a consensus-based checklist that identifies common pitfalls and consolidates best practices for researchers adopting AI, and a benchmark to foster the development of AI agents that can verify scientific reproducibility. AI evaluation failures affect several other applications. Beyond science, he examines how AI agent benchmarks miss many failure modes, and present HAL, a system to address evaluation shortcomings and conduct large-scale agent evaluations.The talk examines inference scaling, a recent technique to boost AI capabilities, and show that many claims of improvement fail to hold under realistic conditions. Finally, Kapoor discusses how better AI evaluation can inform policymaking, drawing on work on open foundation models and engagement with state and federal agencies.Why does the evaluation crisis persist? The AI community has poured enormous resources into building evaluations for models, but not into investigating how models impact the world. To address the crisis we need to build a systematic science of AI evaluation to bridge the gap between benchmark performance and real-world impact.

events.title: Tanner Lectures on Human Values with Amia Srinivasan (Oxford University) - "Psyche and the City"
events.description: Lecture I: Politics on the CouchAbstract for Professor Srinivasan's lectures:AmiaSrinivasan'slectures will explore the intersection of psychoanalysis and politics, tracing how thinkers from Freud to contemporary feminists have grappled with the potential of psychoanalysis to liberate not just individuals but societies. In her first lecture, Srinivasan will examine whether psychoanalysis can inform political discourse, reconcile justice with universal trauma, and balance structural critique with individual complexity. Her second lecture will revisit Freud’s controversial shift from seduction theory to the Oedipus Complex, questioning the implications of privileging psychic reality over objective truth. Together, the lectures will ask whether psychoanalysis can deepen our understanding of trauma, identity, and freedom in political life.Commentators:Two commentators follow each lecture (all commentators are with us both days):Cheshire Calhoun, Professor of Philosophy Emerit, Arizona State University;Dagmar Herzog, Distinguished Professor, History, Social Welfare, Women’s and Gender Studies, City University of New York;Mark Lilla, Professor of Humanities, Columbia University;Jacqueline Rose, Professor of Humanities and the London Critical Theory Summer School, Birbeck, University of London.
events.speaker: Amia Srinivasan
